model: Ideal transfer algebra (agentkit.mesh, agentkit.mzi) plus an explicit planar crossing layout and a parametric worst-path loss model. No geometry, no measured device.
hypothesis_under_test: H-B (guide v2 section 39): for structured non-universal transforms (radix-2 butterfly, DFT), 3D routing removes the crossings a planar layout needs and reduces worst-path loss and error at equal N.

fixed_parameters.U_db_label: ASSUMPTION: planning value for the repeatability of an insertion-loss difference between two fiber-coupled chips

interpretation_rules.I1: XC = lowest verified per-crossing insertion loss for fs-written glass waveguides from T26 rule R4. If XC >= breakeven(N = 16) = 2 U / worst-path crossings(16), the crossing advantage of 3D is predicted to be measurable at N = 16 and H-B is retained as a candidate. If XC < breakeven(16), H-B is retained only for the smallest N with worst-path crossings x XC >= 2 U, and withdrawn as a headline if that N exceeds 64. If T26 verifies no XC, the crossing loss is declared the decisive unknown and H-B stays open.
interpretation_rules.I2: Error accumulation (Clements versus butterfly DFT) is reported descriptively; no threshold.
interpretation_rules.I3: Against a planar Clements mesh (no crossings, universal), the 3D butterfly saves N - log2 N stages; reported on the loss grid. Universality is lost and this is stated.

pre_commit_checks: Software smoke test only: crossing counts and DP versus brute force for N = 4 and 8, FFT factorization for N = 4. No other output was computed before this commitment.
heldout_policy: Deterministic model; no data split. Seeds fixed above.
